items.title: Missiles hit Kyiv after Russia agrees to US call to resume Ukraine peace talks
items.description: Russia says it is "ready in principle" to resume peace talks and US President Donald Trump says the world is "the closest we've been" to ending the war.

items.title: Rosenberg: US diplomatic push offers little hope for imminent Ukraine peace
items.description: Russia's President Putin does not feel under pressure right now to end the war.

items.title: Macron accuses foreign leaders of exploiting French riots
items.description: The comment is an apparent swipe at Benjamin Netanyahu and Donald Trump, who both face elections in coming weeks.

items.title: Pope does not need further treatment after lung cancer surgery
items.description: Test results have confirmed his diagnosis as a lung adenocarcinoma that was localised.

items.title: 'Targeted' attack on much-loved MP leaves Australian town heartbroken
items.description: Locals describe the MP, who had to have both legs amputated, as a genuinely kind person who fought for the community.

items.title: Family of prison officer killed by IRA receives state apology
items.description: Brian Stack was crossing a street in Dublin in 1983 when he was shot in the back of the neck and died 18 months later.

items.title: Ex-prosecutor charged with treason in Mexico over US drug raid
items.description: César Jáuregui Moreno is accused of allowing US agents to join a raid on a suspected drugs lab in April.

items.title: Pakistan arrests man wanted by US over $126m postage fraud case
items.description: Faheem Akram allegedly sold more than 5 million fake postage labels for a fixed price of $2 a piece.

items.title: Meta fined $25bn for 'lies' over user data privacy
items.description: The fine is the largest to date against Facebook's owner, larger than an $18bn deal with California.

items.title: Nigeria's first Ebola patient holidayed in Uganda, officials say
items.description: The wife of a diplomat based in Abuja travelled to Kampala for a vacation.

items.title: India 'cockroach' leaders who called on election chief to quit are freed from jail
items.description: Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were accused of breaking into an unauthorised protest venue in Delhi.

items.title: Elon Musk confirms he is considering merging Tesla and SpaceX
items.description: Musk says special committees within both companies have been formed to look at a possible mega-merger.

items.title: Gambia to pay victims of Yahya Jammeh's rule from proceeds of his seized US mansion
items.description: The Gambia has confirmed receiving $2.5m from the sale of the house in Maryland.

items.title: Sudan army drones hit mourners and fuel market killing more than 300 people, sources say
items.description: A truck carrying people to a funeral and a market alleged to be supplying fuel to the RSF were targeted.

items.title: Trump and Zelensky at loggerheads despite new optimism
items.description: The Ukrainian leader's hug with Steve Witkoff in the Norwegian capital is unlikely to dispel misgivings about US policy towards his country, writes Paul Adams.

items.title: Alberta's decisive decision to stay in Canada gives Carney backing to take on Trump
items.description: The overwhelming vote by Alberta to stay in Canada gives Mark Carney political capital to focus on remaking the country's economy, writes the BBC's Lyse Doucet.

items.title: Swimmer, 65, killed in shark attack off South Africa's east coast
items.description: Janine Lochrenberg, 65, was out on her daily morning swim with her club when she was attacked, her family tell the BBC.

items.title: Trump sued over Canadian tariffs in latest legal challenge
items.description: The lawsuit argues the White House exceeded its authority in imposing the latest tariffs on the country and caused "immediate harm to American businesses".

items.title: North Korea publishes photos of Kim Jong Un - why do rumours of his death keep coming back?
items.description: North Korean state media has published photos of the dictator with his daughter after the unsubstantiated rumour spread.

items.title: Tourist found guilty after stealing Las Vegas flamingo from enclosure
items.description: The man testified that he snatched Peachy from its enclosure at the Flamingo hotel and casino after drinking 30 to 40 beers, but did not mean any harm.
